To be Dumb

June 13, 2026

What dumb really means

  • totally subjective
  • self perception of dumbness

I have often thought of myself as the dumb one of the bunch. My self-assessment as the dumb one has carried its way from as early as I can remember, and continues through my present employment. The essay here is not a cry for help, or an invitation to a pity party. The words here are not a flogging, a public display of self deprecation. From conversations I’ve had with loved ones, coworkers, and strangers, I hope nothing I say is controversial in any way and serves only as a musing on what it means to be alive now with just enough knowledge equipped to reckon with the vastness of intelligent space.

It is wholly impossible to measure dumbness. Dumbness is different than anti-intelligence, which is also impossible to measure though we as humans can’t help but try. Wheras intelligence is possibly some quality of how quickly information leads to knowledge or positive reinforcement, dumbness is a static variable. To be dumb is mortal. To be dumb is inescapable, a force of cosmic goo which grips the ankles and holds on for eternity against the struggle of those who are dumb and wish not to be.
